record.paper_title: Open problems for the superKdV equations
record.original_question: Why are there exactly three integrable N = 2 supersymmetric Korteweg-de Vries extensions, and is there an underlying Lie-algebraic explanation for this threefold classification, for example one connected to the existence of three classical algebras?

evidence.quote: OP-6: Why is there exactly three integrable N = 2 super KdV extensions? Is there an underlying Lie algebraic interpretation for this threefold way (i.e, is this related to the existence of the three classical algebras)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
The N=2 supersymmetric Korteweg–de Vries (super-KdV) equation is an evolution equation for an N=2 superfield Φ(x,θ₁,θ₂,t) = w(x,t) + (fermionic terms) + θ₁θ₂ u(x,t), where the bosonic component u reduces, in the appropriate limit, to the KdV variable. Consider the one-parameter family of N=2 supersymmetric extensions of KdV
   Φ_t = −Φ_xxx + 3(Φ D₁D₂Φ)_x + ((a−1)/2)(D₁D₂Φ²)_x + 3aΦ²Φ_x,
where D₁, D₂ are the standard N=2 odd covariant derivatives and a is a real parameter. It is a classical result that this family admits an infinite hierarchy of local conserved charges (and hence is integrable in the Lax/bi-Hamiltonian sense) for exactly three values of the parameter, namely a ∈ {−2, 1, 4}.

Prove or disprove: there is a Lie-algebraic explanation for why exactly these three values yield integrable N=2 super-KdV hierarchies. In particular, determine whether this threefold classification can be put in natural bijection with the three infinite series of classical (simple) Lie algebras, or otherwise identify the algebraic structure (e.g. affine Lie superalgebra, Drinfeld–Sokolov-type reduction, or loop algebra grading) that intrinsically singles out the three integrable cases a = −2, 1, 4.
artifact.status_search_result: The literature confirms that exactly three values a = −2, 1, 4 give integrable N=2 super-KdV extensions, and various Lie-(super)algebraic constructions have been proposed (e.g. Drinfeld–Sokolov reductions of sl(2,2)^(1), sl(2,1)-based mKdV/Miura formulations, and classifications via odd-grade generators in loop superalgebras). However, no single accepted Lie-algebraic explanation deriving the threefold classification from "three classical algebras" has been established; partial constructions exist but a complete intrinsic Lie-algebraic interpretation remains an open question.

status_evidence.title: Supersymmetry and the KdV equations for integrable hierarchies with a half-integer gradation
status_evidence.snippet: Classification scheme of supersymmetric integrable models in terms of constant odd integer grade generators of a loop algebra squaring to a semisimple element.
status_evidence.claim: Lie-algebraic frameworks have been proposed but do not yet uniquely explain the three N=2 super-KdV cases.

status_evidence.title: Integrable extensions of N=2 supersymmetric KdV hierarchy
status_evidence.snippet: Integrable extensions arising from nonuniqueness of roots of the Lax operator.
status_evidence.claim: Multiple constructions exist; threefold classification not fully reduced to a single algebraic origin.
